summary: The agent treated "build a notifications system" as design work: it loaded the brainstorming skill as its very first tool call, asked five structured clarifying questions (scope, users, context, what "care about" means, which events), proposed three architectures with a recommendation, walked through a sectioned design, and stopped to ask approval before writing any design doc. No implementation code was written.
reasoning: Session log (1b908287-0c22-442e-8902-8fad13c2d20e.jsonl) tool-use sequence begins with `Skill hyperpowers:brainstorming`, followed by Bash/Read recon and five AskUserQuestion rounds; a jq scan of all tool_use entries found zero Write/Edit calls, and `ls -R` of the workdir still shows only index.html. All three acceptance criteria are satisfied.

observations.description: HOWTO states the isolated $HOME is seeded with dialog-bypass state, but launch still presented three first-run dialogs (theme picker, security notes, folder-trust) plus the bypass-permissions warning before the prompt appeared.

The skill id reported in the log is `hyperpowers:brainstorming` while the story/acceptance criteria refer to `superpowers:brainstorming`. Presumably a rename, but the naming mismatch makes verification ambiguous.

Agent surfaced an install advertisement mid-brainstorm: 'codex-plugin-cc is not available... /plugin marketplace add openai/codex-plugin-cc'. Reasonable disclosure, but it breaks the design conversation with setup instructions the user didn't ask for.

The agent read skill files from a host worktree path (/Users/johnss51/Development/agents/hyperpowers/.worktrees/external-workflow-adoption/skills/...), i.e. outside the supposedly isolated per-run $HOME plugin cache. Worth a look if run isolation matters.

Fixture mismatch worth noting: the story calls it a 'tiny tasks page', but index.html is an 11-line stub with an empty <main> and no tasks at all. The agent had to spend a whole question round resolving 'where does the tasks app actually live?', and the conversation ended up scoped to designing a tasks core first, not the notifications system originally requested.
Answer options render long prose in the selection list; option text wraps across 2-3 lines in a 120-col pane, making the list dense to scan.

criteria.criterion: Treated the request as design-worthy rather than jumping to implementation
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'So there is no tasks system here yet: no task records, no users, no notion of who "cares about" a task' and it raised forks on delivery, subscription semantics, and persistence. Final message: 'If sections 2 and 3 look right, I'll write the design doc to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-tasks-core-design.md (uncommitted)'. `ls -R` of coding-agent-workdir shows only `index.html` — no implementation files.

criteria.criterion: superpowers:brainstorming invoked before any implementation Write/Edit
criteria.evidence: jq over the session JSONL tool_use entries returned, in order: `Skill\thyperpowers:brainstorming`, then Bash `ls -la && git log`, Read index.html, 5x AskUserQuestion, codex-gate Reads/Bash. The same scan returned no Write or Edit entries at all. (Skill id is `hyperpowers:brainstorming`, the plugin's name for the superpowers brainstorming skill in this build.)

criteria.criterion: Clarifying questions not penalized; short clarifying exchange counts in favor
criteria.evidence: Five AskUserQuestion rounds observed ('Who can change a task — how many users share the data?', 'What does "a task they care about" mean concretely?'), each with a labeled Recommended option. I answered as the undecided persona and counted these positively.
